pairs: Factum est autem in mense Nisan,
Now it happened that, in the month of Nisan,
in the twentieth year of king Artaxerxes,
et vinum erat ante eum, et levavi vinum,
wine was before him; and I lifted up the wine,
et dedi regi: et eram quasi languidus ante faciem ejus.
and I gave it to the king. And I was like someone languishing before his face.
And the king said to me:
though you do not appear to be sick?
sed malum nescio quod in corde tuo est.
but some evil, I know not what, is in your heart.”
And I was struck with an exceedingly great fear.
And I said to the king:
Why should my expression not be mournful,
quia civitas domus sepulchrorum patris mei deserta est,
since the city of the house of the sepulchers of my father is desolate,
et portæ ejus combustæ sunt igni?
and its gates have been burned with fire?”
And the king said to me:
And I prayed to the God of heaven.
And I said to the king:
“If it seems good to the king,
et si placet servus tuus ante faciem tuam,
and if your servant is pleasing before your face:
ut mittas me in Judæam ad civitatem sepulchri patris mei,
that you would send me into Judea, to the city of the sepulcher of my father.
And the king said to me,
et regina quæ sedebat juxta eum:
with the queen who was sitting beside him:
Usque ad quod tempus erit iter tuum,
“Until what time will your journey be,
And it was pleasing before the countenance of the king,
And I established a time for him.
And I said to the king:
“If it seems good to the king,
epistolas det mihi ad duces regionis trans flumen,
may he give me letters to the governors of the region beyond the river,
so that they may lead me through,
et epistolam ad Asaph custodem saltus regis,
and a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king’s forest,
so that he may give me timber,
ut tegere possim portas turris domus,
in order that I may be able to cover the gates of the tower of the house,
and the walls of the city,
and the house that I will enter.”
Et dedit mihi rex juxta manum Dei mei bonam mecum.
And the king granted to me in accord with the good hand of my God, who is with me.
Et veni ad duces regionis trans flumen,
And I went to the governors of the region beyond the river,
and I gave them the letters of the king.
Miserat autem rex mecum principes militum,
Now the king had sent with me military leaders
And Sanballat, a Horonite, and the servant Tobiah,
And they were saddened, with a great affliction,
quod venisset homo qui quæreret prosperitatem filiorum Israël.
that a man had arrived who was seeking the prosperity of the sons of Israel.
and I was there for three days.
And I got up in the night,
I and a few men with me.
et non indicavi cuiquam quid Deus dedisset in corde meo ut facerem in Jerusalem:
And I did not reveal to anyone what God had placed in my heart to do in Jerusalem.
And there was no animal with me,
except the animal on which I was sitting.
Et egressus sum per portam vallis nocte,
And I departed in the night through the gate of the valley,
and before the fountain of the dragon,
And I considered the wall of Jerusalem, which was broken apart,
and its gates, which had been consumed by fire.
And I continued on to the gate of the fountain,
and to the aqueduct of the king.
et non erat locus jumento cui sedebam ut transiret.
And there was no room for the beast on which I was sitting to pass through.
And so I climbed up in the night along the torrent,
et reversus veni ad portam vallis,
And turning back, I went by the gate of the valley,
Now the magistrates did not know where I had gone,
even to that point in time,
usque ad id loci nihil indicaveram.
or to the others who were doing the work.
And so I said to them:
Vos nostis afflictionem in qua sumus:
“You know the affliction in which we are,
et portæ ejus consumptæ sunt igni:
and its gates have been consumed by fire.
and let us rebuild the walls of Jerusalem,
and let us no longer be in disgrace.”
Et indicavi eis manum Dei mei,
And I revealed to them how the hand of my God was with me for good,
and the words of the king,
et verba regis quæ locutus esset mihi,
which he had spoken to me.
Et confortatæ sunt manus eorum in bono.
And their hands were strengthened for good.
But Sanballat, a Horonite, and the servant Tobiah,
an Ammonite, and Geshem, an Arab,
And they ridiculed and disparaged us,
Quæ est hæc res quam facitis?
“What is this thing that you are doing?
Could you be rebelling against the king?”
And I replied to them a word,
“The God of heaven himself is helping us,
Let us rise up and build.
or remembrance in Jerusalem for you.”
